video_title: NBA Finals Preview: Who Has More PRESSURE? Players to Watch | OKC Offseason & Contract Situation

quotes.speaker: Paul Pierce
quotes.summary_phrase: Paul Pierce and Wosny Lambre debate the best player in the league
quotes.excerpt: To me it's Victor for sure.

text_blocks.speaker: Wosny Lambre
text_blocks.text: Everybody in the league, who you taking number one?

text_blocks.speaker: Paul Pierce
text_blocks.text: I don't even think you can argue with that. Joker? No. To me it's Victor for sure.

quotes.speaker: Danny Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Danny Green highlights De'Aaron Fox as a key player for the Spurs
quotes.excerpt: He was a 1A before he got there, it's Fox. He's going to be very important.
quotes.quote: For me in San Antonio, he shouldn't be a role player. He was a 1A before he got there, it's Fox. He's going to be very important to the series. Some people mention him, but they mention him in the same breath as they do Dillon Brooks, Stephon Castle, Wembanyama. They have him as like an add-on, but I'm like this guy was a 1A before he got there and he could definitely be a 1B or a two when given the right opportunity and moments and when he's aggressive and shows it.

quotes.speaker: Danny Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Danny Green identifies Duop Reath as a potential X-factor for the Knicks
quotes.excerpt: I feel like Duop Reath could be that guy.
quotes.quote: On the Knicks side, I feel like Duop Reath could be that guy. Landry Shamet has gotten a lot of that love and light for good reason. Of course Mitchell Robinson, Josh Hart, like all those other guys, but Duop Reath, he was in that Philly series, he was big time and even in the Cleveland series, there's moments he had moments that was huge for them and he could be a guy that can light it up and that can change a game, change a series for you if he gets hot.

quotes.speaker: Paul Pierce
quotes.summary_phrase: Paul Pierce emphasizes the importance of glue guys in championship teams
quotes.excerpt: Every championship team has a glue guy, has an X-factor.
quotes.quote: For me, on the San Antonio side, every championship team has a glue guy, has an X-factor. I like James Posey for the Boston Celtics, I like a Robert Horry, I like guys that just come in and just hit big shots and are forever, just Steve Kerr on the Bulls. There's always guys like that every year and for me, for San Antonio, there's going to be a guy and they have a number of them. They got about five, six guys like that.

quotes.speaker: Paul Pierce
quotes.summary_phrase: Paul Pierce names Josh Hart as the X-factor for the Knicks
quotes.excerpt: It has to be Josh Hart.
quotes.quote: It has to be Josh Hart. It has to be Josh Hart and we saw that in that game-clinching win versus Cleveland how Josh Hart just stepped up because teams leave him open. They respect OG, they respect Towns, they respect Brunson, they respect Bridges for what they've done. Now they're saying because they not that they don't respect Josh Hart, it's just like if I'm going to leave somebody open out of these five, it's going to be Josh Hart. So he's going to have ample opportunity to be that X-factor if the Knicks are going to win this series.

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: Wosny Lambre discusses the role players' importance for the Knicks
quotes.excerpt: Those two guys definitely and of course and like you said Josh Hart.
quotes.quote: I'm actually going to echo Danny's sentiments with Shamet and Duop Reath and that's because again if Josh Hart isn't making shots or for whatever reason, Mike Brown decides he wants to go with a lineup that has more shooting just available, maybe Josh Hart is doing well, but they might want to go with a different approach. Those guys not only have to make shots, but they have to hold up on defense too. And we saw Landry Shamet do a great job against Donovan Mitchell last round, he stepped up to the challenge, did a great job moving his feet, being aggressive, being physical. Duop Reath has had his moments, but the Spurs guards are so physical on the ball, they're so much bigger than Duop Reath is, that's going to be a matchup I think to watch.

quotes.speaker: Danny Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Danny Green discusses the pressure of the NBA playoffs
quotes.excerpt: Obviously the stages get bigger, the lights get brighter, the cameras, there's more media tension.
quotes.quote: When it comes down to the pressure and the moments, obviously the stages get bigger, the lights get brighter, the cameras, there's more media tension as you go further in the Western Conference Finals, Eastern Conference Finals and then the Finals. And Wembanyama had some really good things to say, like he finds a way to turn the negatives into a positive. He's like, you know, they're like, why you need to win right now? Why is it, you know, like it's like if it if it's to, what did he say? Something that I'm winning like my life depends on it. Why is it when your life depends on it? He's like, I'm impatient and sometimes impatience can be a virtue and sometimes inexperience can be to an advantage if you play like you have like you have no idea what's going on and it can be reckless, I mean, say reckless, but like, you know, not letting the moment get a hold of you.

quotes.speaker: Paul Pierce
quotes.summary_phrase: Paul Pierce argues the Knicks have the most pressure in the Finals
quotes.excerpt: It's clearly the Knicks.
quotes.quote: So the question is, who is under the most pressure to perform in the Finals? It's clearly the Knicks. I mean, come on, they haven't won a championship in 50 plus years. They haven't been to the Finals in over 26 years. I mean, clearly the Mecca of basketball is New York. Do you see what the streets look like? They're partying, they're parading, the conference championship. Like the the I just went out the other day, the other night, went to a rooftop, New York cats coming up to me, Paul, you talking that about New York. I'm telling you, we going to get this son. Hey son. Like like come on man. It don't get no better than that. If they not feeling the pressure in New York to feel like they have to win this championship, then I don't know what type of pressure. Like who, if we're talking, it's the Knicks. It's not even close.

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: Wosny Lambre discusses the burden on Victor Wembanyama
quotes.excerpt: I think Wembanyama individually has the most shoulders, the most burden.
quotes.quote: It's interesting because it's it you know, it's all on how you look at it, right? Like because I think Wembanyama individually has the most shoulders, the most burden because he is anchoring the defense as well as the offense now. Like the offense kind of runs through him now too. So he's asked to do more than any individual player on the team. On the flip side, man, you know, there's a guy named Giannis Antetokounmpo out there who's been rumored and affiliation with a trade to your team and if you're a guy like Mikal Bridges, Carl-Anthony Towns, even OG Anunoby, you know, um, you got to think you're kind of playing for your New York life in this series because God knows if this doesn't work out, they're going to be like, oh, we need to get Brunson out of here. That's not going to be the case. They're going to be talking about the rest of y'all.

quotes.speaker: Danny Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Danny Green discusses the pressure on teams with high expectations
quotes.excerpt: That's most every major city like team with high expectations.
quotes.quote: That's most every major city like team with high expectations. The teams in big cities will have high expectations and when you get some right pieces and things don't go well, they're looking to make major moves. You know what I'm saying? Even if you're doing, when we won, they they made changes. So it happens and it depends on I guess scenario on who is the main star. When you're over a LeBron James, I've seen a lot of changes happen every year, mid-year, summers. But yes, this is probably an anomaly where you don't see many cases like this for sure.

quotes.speaker: Paul Pierce
quotes.summary_phrase: Paul Pierce describes the intense pressure of playing in New York
quotes.excerpt: There's no other city or team or franchise that had this type of like pressure on them.
quotes.quote: There's no other city or team or franchise that had this type of like pressure on them because it can go from, we're going to name a street after you, we're going to build you a statue, you going to have front row seats for the rest of your life when you retire, you can eat at any restaurant for free, to like, don't you ever bring your ass back to this city. That's the extreme of this Finals, right?

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: Wosny Lambre asks for predictions for the series
quotes.excerpt: Who wins this series in how many games?
quotes.quote: Who wins this series in how many games?

quotes.speaker: Danny Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Danny Green predicts a competitive series between Spurs and Knicks
quotes.excerpt: Whoever wins game five is going to win game six and that's who the winner is.
quotes.quote: I think the Spurs get one the first game, I think they split in San Antonio, I think they split in the garden and I think it goes 50/50. Whoever wins game five is going to win game six and that's who the winner is.

quotes.speaker: Danny Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Danny Green analyzes the Knicks' momentum and health advantage
quotes.excerpt: This Knicks team had a lot of rest, they're pretty healthy and they're on a win streak.
quotes.quote: But before the series, I picked the Knicks because they're playing really good basketball. Again, some of the best teams in the world don't win a championship, it's who's playing the best basketball at that moment and who's the healthiest. I think San Antonio is beat up a little bit, they're tired, fatigued. Again, you did the pod with KG talking about his emotions coming out, maybe he was too emotional, can he get over that emotional high? And could those young guys be ready for this moment? I don't know. This Knicks team had a lot of rest, they're pretty healthy and they're on a win streak that's unbelievable. Like they're point differential 27 points beating teams up like and they're playing together. Like this is a Knicks team that had beaten them in the regular season, which I know doesn't matter as much, it is the regular season, but they're better, they're what they are in the regular season. Both teams are better, but it's hard for me not to pick a team that's rolling like that. And again, I'm not a Knicks fan, but to see them playing in this way, it's hard for me to root against them or think that they can't win a series. So I'm going to stick with my prediction that I had before the series, that's what I had before the series, I'm going to stick with it and I hope that I'm wrong.

quotes.speaker: Paul Pierce
quotes.summary_phrase: Paul Pierce predicts the Spurs will win the series
quotes.excerpt: I'm going with the team and the guy who visited the Monks, KG, Jamal Crawford, Hakeem Olajuwon.
quotes.quote: I'm going with the team and the guy who visited the Monks, KG, Jamal Crawford, Hakeem Olajuwon. He swam underwater with weights. He walked up a hill dribbling a basketball. Come on man, it don't get no better than that. We're talking about a man that really wants it. The man went on a press conference and said, I want this more. My life depends on it. I'm rocking with a dude who talking like that. That sound like some KG type of, my life, that sound like some Kobe type of press conference. That sound like some Jordan type of, he's willing to die for this. I'm taking a guy that has that type of mentality in the series and there's no, like you can't tell me nothing.

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: Wosny Lambre analyzes the Spurs' roster and potential
quotes.excerpt: They do have the components to challenge what San Antonio does well.
quotes.quote: They do have the components to challenge what San Antonio does well in terms of Wembanyama with his size and the guard penetration. They have so many good wing defenders, they have the bigs to to contest with Wembanyama size, they have the rebounding, they have a closer in Jaylen Brown, they have ways to play multiple, they're showing you multiple ways, transition, offensive rebounds. We're doing our flex actions, we're killing you in isolation. They have so many ways to attack, it just feels like everything is lining up for this team and so yeah, I like the Knicks in six and I actually do think like the Knicks to still game one. I think they got to get game one in order to wrong foot San Antonio and then I do think they win three out of the next five games after that and go on to become the world champions.

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: Wosny Lambre discusses Victor Wembanyama's rebounding potential
quotes.excerpt: Victor Wembanyama is averaging 11.3 rebounds.
quotes.quote: Victor Wembanyama is averaging 11.3 rebounds. DraftKings Sportsbook has him at a plus 122 for 14 or more rebounds, Danny, what do you think about that one? 14 reps. I think that's I think that's very high, especially with the fact that he had some issues with Hartstein. If they, if Mitchell Robinson is cleared to play, which is again, he said he plans on playing, the doctors and the Knicks have to clear him. That's what's going to depend on it. If he's cleared to play and he plays 20 plus minutes, I think that rebound number, I'm going to say under, but if he doesn't play then I'll go over, but I'm expecting Mitchell Rob to play and I'm going to say I'm going to say under on that 14, that's a lot of rebounds. He hasn't gotten that since game two of the Western Conference Finals.

quotes.speaker: Paul Pierce
quotes.summary_phrase: Paul Pierce predicts Victor Wembanyama will exceed rebounding expectations
quotes.excerpt: I'm going over everything Wembanyama does.
quotes.quote: I'm going over everything Wembanyama does. I'm going to go under 14, just seems like a lot. Um, and he will and I think the Knicks will ask him to play on the perimeter a lot, which will take him away from the basket, his teammates are going to have to gang rebound and so I'm I'm going to go a little under on the 14 plus at a plus 122.

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: Wosny Lambre discusses Victor Wembanyama's scoring potential
quotes.excerpt: Victor Wembanyama averaging 24.5 points coming into this game.
quotes.quote: Victor Wembanyama averaging 24.5 points coming into this game, 28 plus at a minus 108, Danny, that means he's favored to get 28 or more. That's hot, that's hot. But I think he'll score more than he'll rebound because he also, he'll be fresh, he'll be rested. Like even though they went seven game series, they got a good amount of days off. He hasn't had that many days in a long time. So I'm going to say he he gets right at 28, like I think he'll get the over. He'll score quite a bit. I don't know if he'll rebound the well though. So I'll go over for this one.

quotes.speaker: Paul Pierce
quotes.summary_phrase: Paul Pierce predicts Victor Wembanyama will score over 28 points
quotes.excerpt: Over everything Wembanyama does.
quotes.quote: Over everything Wembanyama does. This is crazy because I I guess I'm just blind. I don't I don't know. I don't know what it is because I don't know what's going on with y'all, but I don't know how y'all don't see greatness when it's sitting right in front of y'all. Like this kid is tremendous. Yes he is. Like a bad night for him was 20 and eight. If he just plays decent, that's 25 and 15. Great is 40 and 20.
